narrative.overview:
A night highway seen from above, photographed on a long exposure: gold headlight trails one way, red taillights the other, and Ed's car in the middle. Everything else on the page is the hotel stationery you'd find in the glovebox of that drive: ivory paper, thin gold rules, a serif that looks engraved. The pace is calm and unhurried; nothing pops, things drift.

The page alternates two grounds, deep green night and ivory paper, joined by wavy lane-line seams. Structure comes from rules and type, not from boxes: lists are ruled, sections are full-bleed, and only two objects on the whole page are cards (the rates stationery and the estimate form). Type is big for a 60+ reader on a phone: body never under 17px, primary actions 60px tall.

Motion belongs to the road. The hero canvas, the lane seams and the step car are the only moving things, and every one of them stops for reduced motion and when off screen.
keyCharacteristics: Deep Irish green ground, never black; ivory and paper for reading sections.
Cormorant display with one gold italic turn of phrase per heading; system sans for everything read or tapped.
Thin gold rules and dashed gold lane markings as the only ornament.
Pill buttons, gold on green, green on ivory; hover and focus share one outline ring.
Taillight red lives only inside the motion (canvas, still-frame trails).

rules.name: The Never-Black Rule
rules.body: The darkest value on the page is ground-deepest. No `#000`, no neutral greys; shadows are tinted from the ground green. The canvas car and the step car's drop shadow use black at 35-45% alpha; that is illustration paint, not a precedent for UI shadows.

rules.name: The Ground-Matched Gold Rule
rules.body: On green, use gold; on ivory or paper, use gold-deep. Same for rules (rule-dark vs rule-light) and text (cream vs ink). Every element picks its pair from the ground it sits on, never across.

rules.name: The Red-Stays-On-The-Road Rule
rules.body: Taillight red appears only inside moving imagery. It is not an accent color.

rules.name: The One Italic Rule
rules.body: Each heading may turn one phrase italic 500, colored gold (green ground) or gold-deep (ivory). That phrase carries the meaning ("I'll drive.", "full.", "Very reasonable rates."). Never italicize a whole paragraph.

rules.name: The 17px Floor
rules.body: Nothing the customer reads drops below 17px (16px only for the copyright line). Labels are the one smaller register, and they are never sentences.

rules.name: Tight Serif, Loose Sans
rules.body: Serif headings sit at 0.92-1.22 line height; sans copy at 1.5-1.6. The tight leading on display is intentional.

rules.name: The Ruled List Rule
rules.body: Lists of facts (pack, where, trust, FAQ) are rows separated by 1px rules, top rule on the first item, no bullets, no boxes. Row padding 16-24px vertical. On desktop the trust list turns into three columns each topped by one rule.

rules.name: The Sticky Headline Rule
rules.body: In two-column sections where the right column is long (journey, FAQ), the h2 sticks at 96px from the top.

rules.name: The Lit-From-Above Rule
rules.body: Every shadow falls straight down with a negative spread, so it reads as ambient light under an object, never a hard offset or a glow halo.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: Hover and keyboard focus look the same: a 2px outline at 3px offset. Sections set `--ring` (`on-dark`: cream; `on-light` and the form: gold-deep) and every interactive thing (buttons, big number, FAQ summaries, footer and form links, inputs) uses it. Don't introduce color-fill hovers.

dos: **Do** pick color, rule and ring from the ground an element sits on (`on-dark` / `on-light` classes set `--ring`).
**Do** join every new section to its neighbors with a lane-line divider carrying both grounds' hexes.
**Do** keep the primary action a `tel:+17323003835` link, gold on green or green on ivory, 60px tall.
**Do** set facts as ruled lists in serif rows before reaching for cards.
**Do** keep body copy at 18px+ and measures at 30-40ch.
**Do** pause any new animation off screen and give it a reduced-motion still frame.
**Do** put new rates in the stationery card style (paper, double hairline, 6px).
donts: **Don't** use black or neutral grey anywhere, including shadows.
**Don't** use taillight red outside moving imagery.
**Don't** use gold (light) text on ivory or gold-deep on green; it fails contrast on the wrong ground.
**Don't** wrap sections or list rows in cards; the rates card and the estimate form are the only cards.
**Don't** add hover fills or color-swap hovers; hover is the outline ring.
**Don't** let hero copy and light trails overlap; extend the clear-zone instead.
**Don't** start a second rAF loop for something that can join an existing one.
